# Super

> A minimalist front-end framework, typed end to end, that governs three things: stores, components and routing. Everything else belongs to your project.

Version 0.1.0 of the `@super-ts/*` packages, published on npm. Status: exploratory draft, the API may still change (0.x: a minor version can break). Install: `npm i @super-ts/core @super-ts/dom` and `npm i -D @super-ts/vite @super-ts/lang @super-ts/testing`, see [Getting started](getting-started.html#install). Links are relative to the `docs/` folder of the repository.

## Documentation in one file

- [Full documentation](llms-full.txt): all the pages in markdown, code included (421 KB).
- [Short documentation](llms-small.txt): the same, without the references to the examples app or the secondary passages, for small context windows (358 KB).

## Start here

- [Introduction](index.html): A minimalist front-end framework, typed end to end, that governs three things: stores, components and routing. Everything else belongs to your project.
- [Getting started](getting-started.html): Install the repository, run the example, then write a complete feature end to end.
- [Examples](examples.html): Super's examples live in a single app, [`examples/demo`](../examples/demo/). Its home page leads to each one: counters, form, shop, errors, widget, composition, UI kit. This page says which file shows which concept.
- [Architecture](architecture.html): Super imposes two folders and four rules. Everything else in your `src` is user-land: Super does not look at it.

## Stores

- [Contracts](contracts.html): A contract describes a store from the outside: what you can read, what you can ask of it, what it announces. It is the only thing a component knows about a store.
- [Selectors](selectors.html): Selectors are the permitted reads of the state. They are the contract's methods, used as they are by components, the store and tests. You write them with the state as the first parameter, and Super supplies it at call time: you write `count(s, id)` in the contract, then `selectors.count(id)` everywhere else.
- [Stores](stores.html): A store implements a contract. It holds the state, handles the commands, waits for what it has to wait for (an adapter, the network), then updates its state and announces what happened.
- [Commands and events](commands-and-events.html): The view sends and lets go. The store does the work, waits for what it has to wait for, then succeeds or fails. Super tracks each command from end to end: it knows when it is pending, and publishes its outcome.

## Components

- [Components](components.html): A component is a typed custom element, written as a class that extends `SuperElement`. Its declarations and fields prepare the instance once; `render()` displays on every render.
- [Reading a store](reading-a-store.html): `@contract name;` gives the component the view of the store provided by the application. `@selector` chooses what it reads from it: the component only re-renders if that value changes.
- [Local state](local-state.html): Local state belongs to a component instance: private, created with it, lost with it. It is for interface data; the app's data lives in a store.
- [Parents and children](parents-and-children.html): Props go down, events go up. A parent never drives a child by calling its methods: it passes it props, and the child answers with events.
- [Templates](templates.html): A component is written in a `.super` file: TypeScript whose methods contain HTML elements written as statements. Control flow is TypeScript's (`if`, `for`, `switch`), and the whole template is checked by the compiler: props, events, attributes, references.
- [Forms](forms.html): `@form` binds fields to typed values, applies your rules, checks with the server while the user types when needed, and submits through a store command. "Pending" and server errors come from that command's lifecycle.
- [UI kit](ui.html): `@super-ts/ui` gathers the components an app always ends up writing: fields linked to a form, a button that sends a command, a navigation link, messages, windows, menus, a table. They have a plain look controlled by CSS variables, are accessible to the keyboard and to screen readers, and plug straight into Super's contracts, forms and router.

## The application

- [Router](router.html): The router is built into `@super-ts/dom`. Routes are named and typed: a link without its parameter, a value of the wrong type or a wrong query description does not compile. And the router is a store like any other.
- [Errors](errors.html): When a component crashes, Super can show a fallback render in place of the broken part, and report the error in a single place. Three levels, from the most local to the most global: a component's `renderError`, the router's `'!'` screen, and `onError` in the application.
- [Application](application.html): The composition root, `main.ts`, is the only place that chooses the adapters, creates the stores and the router, and provides them to the components.
- [Ports and adapters](ports-adapters.html): External data sources (localStorage, HTTP API, IndexedDB) are not a Super concept: they are plain dependencies of your stores. The [examples app](examples.html) organises them into ports and adapters, a project choice: `localStorage` for the counters, a simulated server for the form, a real HTTP API (dummyjson.com) for the kit's wired table.

## Quality

- [Testing](testing.html): Each building block is tested at its own level: the store without a DOM, the adapter on its own, the component with a fake store, the whole app with an in-memory router. And the typing guarantees have their own tests.
- [Tooling](tooling.html): A `.super` file is not TypeScript that `tsc` or your editor can read on their own. Three tools handle it: the command-line check, the Vite plugin that compiles it, and a language server for the editor. All of them rest on the same principle: a **virtual TypeScript**.
- [Guarantees](guarantees.html): Most misuses of Super are caught before run time: by TypeScript, or by the Vite plugin. This page lists what is checked, where, and what is not.

## Reference

- [API](api.html): Everything Super's packages export, package by package. Each entry links to the page that explains it.
- [FAQ](faq.html): The questions people ask when discovering Super, with a short answer and a link to the details.
- [Limitations](limitations.html): Super is a draft. Here is what it does badly or checks badly today. What it does not do yet is in [Roadmap and open questions](roadmap.html).
- [Roadmap](roadmap.html): What Super lacks for a real app, the follow-ups put aside, and the questions still under discussion. None of this is decided: it is the list the next piece of work will start from. What Super does not do well today is in [Limitations](limitations.html).
